articles.title: Why Most Enterprise Agent Pilots Never Reach Deployment
articles.summary: Deloitte’s 2026 technology trends research estimates that 89% of AI agent pilots fail to reach production. A Teradata survey shows that while 78% of enterprises have at least one agent pilot underway, only 14% have scaled an agent to organization-wide use, highlighting a large gap between experimentation and deployment.
articles.advisor_relevance: The article is useful for framing enterprise AI adoption as broad but still immature, with most agent initiatives not yet translating into scaled deployments. For investors, this suggests near-term AI software monetization may depend less on pilot activity and more on vendors’ ability to help customers operationalize, govern, and scale agent workflows.

articles.title: A Princeton Researcher Proposes Recurrent Looped Transformer (RLT) that Carries Decoder State across Every Token, Fixing 96 Blocks per Token with Unbounded Temporal Depth
articles.summary: A technical report from Princeton researcher Yifan Zhang proposes a Recurrent Looped Transformer architecture that carries decoder state and sliding-window attention cache across prompt and response tokens without resetting at the serving boundary. The design describes a 48-layer encoder and 48-layer decoder configuration with 96 logical blocks per token and an expanding recurrent state path, but no code, model weights, or measured results have been released.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is an early technical proposal rather than a validated commercial development. It may be worth monitoring as part of broader research into more efficient or capable transformer architectures, but the lack of code, weights, benchmarks, or company deployment limits near-term investment relevance.
